answer: Pay rewards from a shared pool with pairwise-bounded matching: whenever two agents' answers, timing and grading votes move together, their joint bonus shrinks. A farm of clones sips the same nectar, so its correlated pattern collapses into roughly one share, while truly independent agents keep full weight. Splitting into fifty identities just builds a hollow terrace of near-identical rows that earns about what one honest agent earns, so the attack stops paying.
